---
applyTo: "src/core/harness/copilot/**, src/core/harness/claude/**, src/core/harness/codex/**, src/core/harness/opencode/**, src/core/harness/qwen/**, src/core/harness/antigravity/**"
---

<purpose>
Harness-specific adapters for CLI execution. Provider directories should contain CLI-specific flags, parsing, hook/MCP setup, and cleanup — not shared orchestration.
</purpose>

<providerResponsibilities>
- Keep each provider focused on its CLI: static `config`, parser(s), notification monitor, permission mapper, log parser, and provider-specific arg building.
- `buildCliArgs()` should handle resolved model/session/workspace/additionalArgs and provider-only flags. Leave prompt assembly, generic hook dispatch, PTY lifecycle, and workflow runtime persistence to shared code.
- `buildHeadlessArgs()` / `buildInteractiveArgs()` are the source of truth for prompt flag/positional ordering. Some CLIs require different prompt placement between modes, so do not push that logic into shared helpers.
- Hook setup now belongs in `buildNotificationHookArgs()` and `buildHeadlessUserHookArgs()`, not inline inside `buildCliArgs()`.
- `CliProviderUtils.getWorkspaceDirs(workspaceRoot, workspaceRoots)` already appends every effective approved external file root (`permissions.allowedExternalFileRoots`, see dev/backlog/ALLOWED_EXTERNAL_FILE_ROOTS_PLAN.md) after workspace folders, for the four providers here that call it (Claude, Codex, Copilot, Antigravity). `permissions.allowedExternalFileRoots` is the sole source of extra `--add-dir` entries — there is no separate `allowedDirs` setting (removed 2026-07-13; it duplicated what external roots now cover). Do not re-fetch or re-append external roots in a provider's own `buildCliArgs()` — that would duplicate `--add-dir` entries. Qwen and OpenCode don't call this helper and are untouched by design (no `--add-dir` equivalent; they rely on their own trust mechanisms for external file references). Copilot's `--allow-all-paths` flag also has no dedicated setting anymore; users pass it via `defaults.additionalArgs["copilot-cli"]` if needed.
</providerResponsibilities>

<statefulProviders>
- Copilot, Claude, and Codex may write temp config/hook artifacts; clean those through `getAdditionalCleanupFilePaths()` and `cleanupWorkspaceArtifacts()` rather than ad hoc deletes in parser/monitor code.
- Qwen mutates shared `.qwen/settings.json` hook state through the shared hooks tracker; register/unregister per workflow. MCP is process-local through `--mcp-config`, so do not reintroduce a settings-file MCP union or an `--allowed-mcp-server-names` workaround.
- OpenCode is intentionally different: MCP, permissions, and the normal completion plugin are delivered through process-local inline configuration/environment. A near-empty CLI permission mapper is expected there; the provider's collision-aware mapper builds the inline permission block.
</statefulProviders>

<parsingAndRecovery>
- Headless and interactive paths must converge on the same `UniversalCliOutput` semantics through one mapping in the provider's `ILogParser`; `headlessSource` is a fidelity choice between stdout and session logs, not a latency choice.
- OpenCode headless output is stdout-sourced JSONL. Never route it through `export`: export is a final snapshot and loses the live event stream.
- Use `augmentParsedOutput()` to patch missing token/session/context-window metadata from logs after the initial parse instead of teaching the UI or `CliIntegration` about provider quirks.
- `extractSessionIdFromLogs()` is a fallback recovery path, not the primary contract.
</parsingAndRecovery>

<gotchas>
- Copilot headless mode unconditionally requests `--output-format json`; its former plain-text response-parser fallback is dead code. Keep any future format fallback in provider metadata, not UI conditionals.
- Claude interactive runs rely on `getInteractiveSpawnEnv()` to remove env that would otherwise block nested Claude execution.
- Claude background-task notifications have two phases in session JSONL: `queue-operation` records only enqueue/dequeue bookkeeping, while a matching `user` task-notification (between turns) or `queued_command` attachment (mid-turn) means Claude actually consumed the resume signal. Never clear `ClaudeLogParser`'s pending-background state from a queue operation: the enqueue can land before the current turn's Stop, with actual delivery and the resumed turn occurring afterward. Track all concurrent task IDs (Claude can notify several independently), treat any tool with `run_in_background: true` as a launch (`PowerShell` as well as `Bash`), and keep a delivered-notification resume latch until the later assistant turn ends; otherwise the catch-up read can clear every task and incorrectly accept the stale Stop that preceded their delivery. `Monitor` is also asynchronous, confirmed by its `Monitor started` tool result. A successful `TaskStop` emits no later task notification, so correlate the launch result's `toolUseResult.backgroundTaskId` back to its tool-use ID and clear that launch from the successful `TaskStop` result; a stopped launch otherwise blocks completion until the Stop-hook monitor times out.
- Copilot CLI background tracking is keyed by async shell IDs: add an ID only from `tool.execution_complete` with `executionMode: "async"`, remove only on a matching `system.notification` (`shell_completed`/`shell_failed`), and keep a notification-to-resumed-turn latch through `assistant.turn_start`/`assistant.turn_end`. A one-check stale-Stop guard is required because the old Stop callback can catch up the notification and complete resumed turn before it checks pending state; the next Stop is the valid completion signal.
- Copilot emits both human steering and injected system reminders as `user.message` records with `delivery: "steering"`, so delivery is not a discriminator. Genuine human messages carry text with no `source`; system reminders carry `source: "system"` (often with only `transformedContent`) and must not become `USER_STEER` output.
- Antigravity log-monitored response content is incrementally sourced from the authoritative `transcript_full.jsonl` (use compact `transcript.jsonl` only when the full file is absent); Go `cli-*.log` supplies session and top-level completion markers. The session watcher must tail both sources independently: resuming a conversation may start a new CLI process while discovery remains attached to the previous process's now-stale Go log, but the stable conversation transcript continues receiving human follow-ups. Pair planner tool calls with the adjacent result line in file order, and treat background-task launches and later `SYSTEM_MESSAGE` completions as separate task-ID events handled by the shared follow-up state. A launch is a `source: "MODEL"` + `type: "GENERIC"` + `status: "RUNNING"` entry (`AntigravityLogParser.trackTranscriptBackgroundState` previously required `type === "RUN_COMMAND"`, which real transcripts never satisfy — the background task launched but was never tracked as pending, so a Stop hook mid-task ended the step early; fixed by matching `GENERIC` instead). A mid-stream `PLANNER_RESPONSE` can also carry `status: "RUNNING"` and must stay excluded, so the check cannot drop the `type` gate entirely. The task ID itself is recovered from freeform content text (`Tool is running as a background task with task id: <id>`), not a structured field. See the note below about agy's current CLI now typing **every** tool result `GENERIC` — including `run_command`, `view_file`, `write_to_file`, MCP, and search results that `AntigravityLogParser`/`AntigravityToolEventBuilder` still expect under distinct per-tool type names.
- agy 1.1.12 (`ANTIGRAVITY_MIN_VERSION`, bumped from 1.0.15) stopped emitting per-tool transcript entry types entirely — `run_command`, `view_file`, `write_to_file`/`replace_file_content`/`multi_replace_file_content`, and `grep_search` results were all confirmed (against a real transcript) to arrive typed `"GENERIC"`, never `RUN_COMMAND`/`VIEW_FILE`/`CODE_ACTION`/`GREP_SEARCH`. `AntigravityLogParser.toolCallMatchesResult`'s `"GENERIC"` case used to *exclude* exactly those tool names (on the assumption they'd carry their own type), so none of them could pair with their originating planner call — `call` stayed `undefined` and they rendered as bare unstructured `TOOL_CALL` events, losing parsed command/diff/exit-code data. Fixed by making the `"GENERIC"` case match unconditionally: since type no longer disambiguates anything, pairing now relies solely on file-order adjacency (oldest pending call wins), consistent with the adjacent-pairing invariant already documented above. `AntigravityToolEventBuilder.build()`'s `RUN_COMMAND` and `CODE_ACTION` branches also needed a `normalizedName`-based fallback (mirroring the one `VIEW_FILE`/`MCP_TOOL`/`SEARCH_WEB` already had) so a paired call still renders as `BASH_COMMAND`/`FILE_WRITE`/`FILE_EDIT` once `result.type` is `GENERIC`. `exitCode()`'s regex was widened to also match agy's real completion phrasing "exited with code N" (previously only "exit code: N"/"exit_code=N"). Unverified against a real transcript: whether `MCP_TOOL`/`LIST_RESOURCES`/`READ_RESOURCE`/`SEARCH_WEB`/`ASK_QUESTION` results (none were exercised by the one real session used to diagnose this) also collapsed to `GENERIC` — the dedicated `case` branches for those are left intact as a safety net in case some still arrive typed, but re-verify against a real transcript that exercises them before trusting that fully. Non-backgrounded (synchronous) `run_command` completions were likewise never exercised by that session, so `parseCommandOutput()`'s `stdout:`/`stderr:` label matching (vs. agy's confirmed `Output:` labeling for background-task completions) is unverified and was deliberately left unchanged rather than guessed at.
- Antigravity writes a `SYSTEM`/`CHECKPOINT` entry containing `{{ CHECKPOINT 0 }}` a few entries into **every** conversation, including brand-new ones where nothing could have been truncated — it is the baseline context scaffold, not a compaction. Its body carries the same "earlier parts of this conversation have been truncated" boilerplate as a real compaction, so only the index discriminates: genuine auto-compaction is `{{ CHECKPOINT 1 }}` and up, lands mid-conversation, and adds a "Previous Session Summary" section. `AntigravityLogParser` drops index 0 (`BASELINE_CHECKPOINT_REGEX`); mapping it would show "Conversation compacted (auto)" at the top of every single run.
- OpenCode must resume with explicit session IDs (`-s`), never “continue last session”.
- When a provider edits workspace files to register hooks/MCP, baseline restoration is more important than eager cleanup because other workflows may still be active.
- Injected prompts bypass CLI argument, hook setup, and the normal execution-sidecar path. Antigravity re-reads its global hook registration when completion events fire, so it opts into `shouldRetainWorkflowArtifactsForReuse()` until the reusable PTY exits. Claude must opt in too: its prompt-scoped `--settings` hook file and global statusline lease must survive with the PTY because Claude hot-reloads settings in running sessions; restoring `~/.claude/settings.json` after deleting the `--settings` file silently removes Stop hooks and statusline reporting from later injected turns. `CliIntegration` must also start a fresh provider execution sidecar around each injected turn so the retained statusline transport is watched again after the prior turn's sidecar stops. Codex deliberately uses the default eager cleanup: its running TUI keeps the already-loaded inline hooks, and retaining generated hook state between executions would trigger trust review prompts on later launches.
- Claude's `AskUserQuestion` tool_result carries `toolUseResult` as an **object** `{questions, answers, annotations}` when answered, but as a bare **string** ("User rejected tool use" / "Error: the user doesn't want to proceed…") when declined — identical to declining any other tool. The answered shape is self-identifying (`isAskUserQuestionResult` in `ClaudeToolBuilder`, keyed on the unambiguous `questions`+`answers` combo), but a decline can only be attributed to `AskUserQuestion` by the *originating tool's name*, which the log doesn't repeat on the `tool_result` block — both `ClaudeLogParser.extractResponse` (a batch-local `pendingToolNames` map) and `extractStructuredEventsFromEvent` (the existing `pendingStreamingToolUses` map) thread tool_use id → name forward for exactly this reason. The "Let's discuss this" decline path is distinguishable from a plain reject only via the sibling `userFeedback` field containing the literal template text "wants to clarify these questions" — there is no structured `declineReason` field. A declined `ASK_USER_QUESTION` event therefore carries no `questions` of its own; `CliEventNormalizer.mergeInitiatedWithCompleted` backfills them from the matching INITIATED event when it collapses the pair into one row.
- Copilot CLI 1.0.x (the 0.0.x → 1.0.x jump) silently dropped the persisted `session.truncation` event entirely, so context-window logic keyed on it goes dark with no error. `events.jsonl` retains `session.shutdown.currentTokens` (system+conversation+toolDefinitions total) but no token limit; do **not** infer the denominator from the model ID because Copilot resolves default vs. long context at runtime. The `CompactionProcessor` utilization line in `~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log` (the other historical fallback) has also become unreliable. When Copilot bumps its CLI version, diff a fresh session log and OTel export against `CopilotLogParser`'s assumptions before trusting existing parsing logic.
- `session.shutdown` only fires when the Copilot **process** exits — and in interactive mode ctrlyoke deliberately keeps that process alive across a multi-step workflow (resumed via `--resume` between steps), so it may not fire until the whole workflow ends. Log-based context tracking is therefore fundamentally insufficient for interactive sessions, independent of the 1.0.x regression above.
- Copilot's OpenTelemetry file exporter (`copilot help monitoring`; `COPILOT_OTEL_ENABLED` + `COPILOT_OTEL_FILE_EXPORTER_PATH`) is the only genuinely live, per-turn context signal left, and `CopilotCliProvider`/`CopilotLogParser` use it as the primary source (see `buildOtelSpawnEnv()`, `pollOtelContextWindow()`, `getFinalOtelUsage()`). Each `chat <model>` span has a nested `github.copilot.session.usage_info` event whose `github.copilot.current_tokens` and `github.copilot.token_limit` attributes are the exact runtime numerator/denominator after Copilot resolves the context tier. Do not substitute the span's `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`: that is billing usage and empirically differs from `current_tokens`. The CLI's SDK defines the equivalent `session.usage_info` event, but marks it ephemeral, so it is normally absent from `events.jsonl`. **Always override the exporter path explicitly per invocation** — some environments have it globally pointed at `\\.\nul`, silently discarding this data. Generate a fresh path in `buildCliArgs()` (or unset it) every prompt because provider/parser instances are reused across prompts within a workflow but are fresh per workflow execution.
- The OTel wiring has two independent consumers: `CliLogMonitor.ts` for interactive/live monitoring and `CopilotCliProvider.augmentParsedOutput()` for headless post-exit enrichment. When adding or changing a context-window signal, wire both paths; otherwise one execution mode silently remains stale even though the exporter file is correct.
- Copilot account quota is a third, separate measurement: `CopilotQuotaClient` sends server-scoped `account.getQuota` over the CLI's JSON-RPC stdio boundary for the authenticated account's monthly entitlement, while OTel `session.usage_info` is the live context-window numerator/denominator and observed per-attempt tokens are separate billing/usage data. Never combine these into one number. The quota probe starts no session and consumes no model turn; treat method-not-found as the `COPILOT_QUOTA_STATUS_CODES.UNSUPPORTED` capability result, not as a CLI-version gate.
- Verified empirically with a real long-lived interactive session (node-pty driving `copilot` directly, two separate turns, process kept alive and idling ~40s+ between/after them): the OTel file exporter flushes each `chat <model>` span **immediately when that turn's API call completes**, not batched until process exit — confirmed by watching file size/span count grow mid-idle, well before the process was killed. So "it only shows 0 in interactive mode" is not an OTel-buffering problem; if you see that symptom, suspect the env/wiring path instead (see `getInteractiveSpawnEnv()` note in `harness-integrations.instructions.md`) before suspecting the exporter itself.
- Antigravity (`agy`) hook and statusline commands are executed with **naive whitespace splitting, no shell quote processing**, and hooks use **cwd = `~/.gemini/config`**. Keep both generated command paths unquoted, absolute, forward-slash, and space-free (`CliNotificationMonitor.buildNodeCommand(..., /*quoted*/ false)`); a quoted or space-containing path reaches node literally and fails before the hook/statusline script runs. The statusline command is stored as `statusLine.command` in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`, while hook commands are stored in `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json`. agy does **not** include the event name in hook stdin (unlike Claude's `hook_event_name`), so `AntigravityNotificationMonitor` passes the native event as **argv[3]** and `ctrlyoke-antigravity-hook.js` derives the logical event from it. Do not alias ctrlyoke `permissionRequest` onto agy's `PreToolUse`: only `preToolUse`/`postToolUse` are wired. For interactive completion use **`Stop`**, not `PostInvocation`, because `PostInvocation` fires per LLM invocation and can signal completion mid-turn. `PreInvocation` (used for `sessionStart`) is per-invocation but harmless because it rewrites the same start file. Verify hook wiring by grepping `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/log/cli-*.log` for `json_hook_caller.go ... executing command` and any following `hook command stderr`.
- `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` is agy-rewritten global state, not a ctrlyoke-owned file: agy may reserialize it on launch, and it reads/caches `statusLine.command` once when each process starts. Keep the statusline lease's baseline restoration and wrap-and-forward behavior intact; changing the file during a running agy process cannot update that process's command.
- Antigravity MCP works (confirmed by manual testing on 1.0.16 — tools were callable) and is enabled unconditionally. `AntigravityCliProvider.getMcpConfigArgs` writes a bare `{ "mcpServers": {...} }` object to the workspace `.agents/mcp_config.json` (agy auto-discovers it, so it returns `[]`, not a CLI arg) via the shared `SettingsJsonMcpTracker` singleton. That tracker was generalized with a `SettingsJsonMcpTrackerOptions` param (`projectConfigPath`/`userConfigPath`) so agy points it at `.agents/mcp_config.json` + `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` instead of the default `.{tool}/settings.json`. agy's server-entry schema differs from Gemini/Qwen — remote servers use **`serverUrl`** (not `url`+`type`) and it recognizes no `trust` field — handled by the `SettingsJsonMcpEntryOptions` (`remoteUrlKey`/`includeRemoteType`/`includeTrust`) on `buildSettingsJsonMcpEntries`. agy has **no `--allowed-mcp-server-names` equivalent**, so parallel workflows in one workspace share the file's servers with no per-prompt scoping. (Historical note: an earlier "MCP hangs agy on startup / non-functional" finding was a mis-diagnosis of the headless working-directory bug — agy headless runs in the home dir and searched there ~10 min for the `.ctrlyoke/temp` prompt file. MCP itself was never the problem.)
- When running `agy` (Antigravity) for testing/verification, **always pass a Gemini Flash tier** (e.g. `--model gemini-3.6-flash-low`). Never let it use agy's own default model (Claude Sonnet): Sonnet has a tiny individual quota that a single run can exhaust (`RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED 429: Individual quota reached. Resets in ~28h`), which blocks the user's real work for a day. Gemini Flash is the cheapest tier with far larger limits. `HARNESS_DEFAULT_MODELS[ANTIGRAVITY_CLI]` is deliberately a Flash tier rather than agy's Sonnet default for this reason — don't "fix" it back to match agy.
- **`agy models` hangs indefinitely under Node's `exec`/`execFile` on Windows** because those leave the child's stdin open as an unwritten, unclosed pipe, and the `models` subcommand specifically blocks reading it before printing anything — confirmed it isn't a general agy startup problem: `agy --version` (used by `AntigravityCliProvider`'s min-version check and `ModelRegistry`'s availability probe) returns in well under a second through the exact same `exec`/`execFile` path. Direct terminal invocation (PowerShell, git-bash) is unaffected, which is why this is easy to miss when spot-checking a command by hand. Both live-discovery call sites (`ModelRegistry.queryAntigravityModels`, `scripts/sync-models.mjs`'s `discoverAntigravityFromCli`) route the `models` call through a local `execWithClosedStdin()` helper (`child_process.spawn` with `stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]`) instead of `execAsync`/`execFileAsync`. If a future agy subcommand query is added and it mysteriously times out only when driven by Node, suspect this same stdin-read behavior before anything else.
- `agy --model` accepts **two vocabularies**: the IDs `agy models` prints (`gemini-3.6-flash-low`) and the display labels its own error output lists (`Gemini 3.6 Flash (Low)`). Both work. ctrlyoke stores **IDs** in `ANTIGRAVITY_CLI_MODELS`, with `ANTIGRAVITY_CLI_MODEL_LABELS` mapping id→label for the dashboard, matching every other harness in `ModelConstants.ts`; it used to store labels with an identity map (migrated 2026-07-26). Two traps when refreshing this list: the effort tier is part of the ID suffix (`-low`/`-medium`/`-high`), *not* agy's separate `--effort` flag, so each tier is its own entry; and `claude-sonnet-4-6` is labelled "(Thinking)" despite having no `-thinking` suffix, unlike `claude-opus-4-6-thinking`. To check an ID without spending inference, pair it with a bogus effort — `agy --model <id> --effort x` reports an invalid-effort error only if the model itself was recognized, since agy validates the model first and rejects unknown ones with exit 1 (it never silently falls back to the default).
- Antigravity headless mode never got a session ID because `AntigravityCliProvider.extractSessionIdFromLogs` keyed its `last_conversations.json` lookup off `process.cwd()` — inside the extension host that is not the workflow's workspace root, so the cache lookup always missed silently (interactive mode was unaffected since it gets `conversationId` straight from the hook payload). Fixed by adding `workspaceRoot` as a third param on `ICliProvider.extractSessionIdFromLogs`, threaded from `runtimeState.getWorkspaceRoot()` (the platform-adapted root, not `process.cwd()`) through `CliResponseCollector.collectHeadlessResponse` / `CliExecutionRunner`, plus a log-scrape fallback (`AntigravityLogParser.extractSessionIdFromLogPath`, scanning the newest `cli-*.log` for the `Print mode: conversation=` / `Starting conversation update stream for` markers) for when the cache hasn't flushed yet or a parallel workflow raced it.
- Antigravity headless stdout is an NDJSON clock/enrichment side-channel, not the content source: `AntigravityCliProvider.headlessSource = "log"` keeps transcript events authoritative because stream-json `tool_info.parameters` omits file content/diffs and command exit codes that `AntigravityToolEventBuilder` reads from transcript `PLANNER_RESPONSE` tool-call args. `CliTransportCoordinator.executeHeadless()` therefore routes those chunks to `HeadlessLogTail`, not the UI stream callback.
- Codex's headless `--json` stream summarises every `file_change` item as `{path, kind}` with **no patch body** — verified constant across every Codex version in this repo's run history, so a "Codex changed their format" theory is the wrong lead. The real change lives only in the session log's `event_msg:patch_apply_end` (`unified_diff` for updates, whole-file `content` for adds/deletes), which is why interactive/log-parsed runs always showed diffs and headless never did. `CodexCliProvider.augmentParsedOutput()` back-fills it. Pair log entries to events **positionally per path**, not first-wins: one path can be changed several times in a turn (add → update → delete), and an INITIATED event describes the same change as the COMPLETED event after it, so only a non-INITIATED event may advance that path's cursor — and a FILE_DELETE must still consume its slot even though it has no body to receive.
- OpenCode's inline config is assembled in two `CliIntegration` phases: `buildCliArgs()` resets the provider's per-prompt accumulator and seeds the plugin, then `prepareToolPermissions()` and MCP setup add their slices before spawn. Preserve that split and reset behavior; `CliIntegration` reuses the provider across prompts and its call order is the reason a provider-local accumulator is safe.
- Codex session `-c` config layers do not merge into one hook array: each layer has its own hook source and positional index space. `CodexInlineHooksBuilder` must therefore compute trust keys from ctrlyoke's emitted groups alone; splicing into a project file would renumber user hooks. A project-local Codex hook that is untrusted is disabled completely silently, so never use the file path as a fallback for completion detection.
- That one `file_change` item type covers all three kinds, so `CodexResponseParser` maps `add`→FILE_WRITE, `delete`→FILE_DELETE, `update`→FILE_EDIT rather than calling everything an edit. This is a correctness fix, not cosmetics: FILE_EDIT undo reverse-patches `structuredPatch`, which a create or delete never has (it failed with "No patch data for reverse-patch"), while FILE_WRITE undo deletes the created file and FILE_DELETE undo restores from the workspace snapshot.
- Diagnosing "this harness shows diffs for some file edits but not others" is misleading, because a FILE_EDIT event is not the only diff source: `getDisplayStructuredPatch` (`webview-react/utils/outputRenderUtils.ts`) falls back to the prompt's `WorkspaceSnapshot` patch, matched by path. That fallback only covers `changeType: "modified"` — `WorkspaceSnapshotService` records created and deleted files with no `structuredPatch` at all — and it is per-attempt and net, so repeated edits to one file within a step all render the same combined diff and it only appears once the step completes. So partial diff coverage can mean the parser is emitting nothing at all and the snapshot is silently covering the modified subset.
- `QwenCliProvider.buildHeadlessArgs()` sends `--input-format stream-json` alongside `--output-format stream-json` — do not remove it as redundant. Qwen has two independent, drifted-apart tool-name alias tables (`packages/core/src/utils/tool-utils.ts`'s older table has no entry for `Write`/`Bash`; `packages/core/src/permissions/rule-parser.ts`'s newer table does, with an explicit `// Claude Code compatibility` comment). Qwen's non-interactive auto-deny gate (`packages/cli/src/config/config.ts`, ~line 1810) checks allow-rule coverage using the *older* table, and — when a run is classified non-interactive (query + `--output-format stream-json` without a matching `--input-format`) with `--approval-mode default`/`auto` — silently force-adds the canonical tool name to the deny list whenever it doesn't recognize ctrlyoke's `Write`/`Bash(...)` allow entries, and deny always wins. The CLI exits 0 with no visible error; the tool call is just rejected as `EXECUTION_DENIED`. `--input-format stream-json` unconditionally skips that gate (`inputFormat !== InputFormat.STREAM_JSON` guard) regardless of interactive classification, which is why it's required for headless. No stdin protocol writing is needed to get this benefit: Qwen auto-wraps the positional prompt into the initial stream-json user message internally, and ctrlyoke's headless spawn already runs with `stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]` (`CliProcessManager.ts`), so Qwen's stream-json stdin reader EOFs immediately and `Session.drainAndShutdown()` still correctly awaits the in-flight turn before exiting — the existing process-exit completion signal is unaffected. Verified empirically against installed CLI v0.20.1. Interactive mode (`buildInteractiveArgs`, the `-i` flag) never sets `--output-format`, so it's never classified non-interactive and never needed this. The pinned real-harness fixture lives in `src/test/harness/inline-config.harness.test.ts` and must be re-verified on upgrade.
- `COPILOT_OTEL_FILE_EXPORTER_PATH` pointed at `\\.\nul` has been observed present in a running process's environment (`Get-ChildItem Env:` / `process.env`) while being absent from both `[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable(name, "User")` and `"Machine")` (i.e. not in the registry at all). This means it isn't a persistent misconfiguration to fix — a process only reads env vars at its own launch time and never re-reads the registry afterwards, so a long-running parent (e.g. the VS Code window itself, and everything it has since spawned, including nested terminals/CLIs) can keep carrying a stale value long after whatever set it was removed. `buildOtelSpawnEnv()`'s unconditional override already neutralizes this for every ctrlyoke-initiated Copilot spawn regardless of ambient state, so don't chase the registry — if the stale value matters for something ctrlyoke doesn't control (e.g. the user manually running `copilot` in an integrated terminal), only a full VS Code restart clears it.
</gotchas>
